artifact: Supplemental independent row-specific E0 review; recommendations only, not coordinator acceptance

input_scope.prior_review: .artifacts/p02/e0-001-035.json (used to detect repeated generic rationales only)

recommendations.rationale: The proposed consumer and demand.arrivals key fit the E0 need for seeded, time-varying arrivals. Keep the profile's rate-versus-timestamped-schedule choice exclusive and make the schedule clock explicit; the row does not justify a value or an arrival distribution.

The ID describes a calendar/seasonal modifier, while the key and schedule-or-interval contract are plausible. The generic rationale incorrectly calls this required; the ID notes applicability remains open and E0's MVP requires time-varying arrivals, not calendar seasonality.
recommendations.replacement: Keep the ID/key and timestamp contract, but change profile_use to optional modifier only when a profile supplies an explicit calendar interval/timezone mapping; omit from minimal deterministic profile.

recommendations.rationale: Surge is a scenario distinction, not a universally required case-mix input. The ID explicitly says distinct surge profiles must not be collapsed without semantic review; the prior acceptance does not address this distinction.
recommendations.replacement: Keep demand.surgeprofile as an optional scenario selector/modifier; require an explicit surge profile definition and leave it absent in minimal and nominal profiles unless selected.

recommendations.rationale: Arrival mode is a categorical case attribute consumed by Flow. Retain it as a typed case attribute when modeled pathways branch on mode; no universal category set or routing policy follows from this row.

Age mix can parameterize case composition, but the current table contract does not say whether categories are mutually exclusive, exhaustive, or conditioned on another attribute. A generic denominator warning does not resolve those structural choices.
recommendations.replacement: Keep demand.agemix optional; require explicit age bands, denominator/population, and conditioning, and validate mutually exclusive/exhaustive categories only where the declared representation requires them.

recommendations.rationale: Case type is a profile classification, but the ID provides no taxonomy or relationship to age/acuity. Treating it as a required generic input could create unsupported clinical groupings.
recommendations.replacement: Keep demand.casetypemix optional and profile-defined; require declared category labels and denominator/conditioning, and do not infer a taxonomy or values.

recommendations.rationale: Acuity is named in E-R1 and E0's source-assumption work, so it has a clear generic pathway consumer. Keep the conditional-table shape and require category labels plus the population denominator; the acceptance asserts no acuity proportions or triage policy.

The ID expressly leaves dependence unspecified. Marginal age, case type, and acuity tables do not establish whether a joint table is needed; accepting this candidate could invite a fabricated dependence structure.
recommendations.replacement: Defer jointcasemix from the minimal profile. Include only after a named profile specifies the joint dimensions, conditioning, denominator, and relationship to supplied marginals.

recommendations.rationale: Referral arrivals are a boundary category, not automatically part of every ED scenario. The generic accept rationale calls all arrival/case-mix inputs required without distinguishing this optional source population.
recommendations.replacement: Keep demand.referrals as an optional boundary-arrival input when the scenario includes referral arrivals; define whether counts mean arrivals or patient proportions and use the declared patient denominator.

recommendations.rationale: This ID concerns transfer arrivals. E0 also models outgoing transfer disposition and external bed offers; those are different flows and should not share an ambiguous transfer concept.
recommendations.replacement: Keep demand.transfers specifically for incoming transfer arrivals and document the source boundary/count denominator; model outgoing transfer as pathways.transfer, not this key.

recommendations.rationale: Repeat presentations need patient linkage and an observation-window definition to distinguish a new presentation from a return by the same person. The parameter ID says those semantics are unresolved, so a generic profile claim is premature.
recommendations.replacement: Defer demand.repeatpresentations from MVP profiles until the contract states linkage key, lookback/window, and whether a repeat is generated as a new arrival or represented by an existing patient history.

recommendations.rationale: Registration is a distinct stage input, but the pathway-stage label alone does not impose clinical content. It can be represented as an optional configured state/transition while retaining patient arrival and registration timestamps separately where the scenario needs them.

Triage and routing are directly relevant to acuity-based pathways. The structured shape is suitable provided routing behavior is separately explicit and category semantics are not invented by the consumer.

Assessment is one of the stages explicitly named in E1's runnable pathway slice. Its structured stage key is suitable, with active work represented through a typed duration input rather than embedded unlabelled elapsed time.

Diagnostics are an explicit E1 stage and can have dependencies. Preserve the structured stage/transition shape, with test ordering and resource waits represented separately from the diagnostic active-work duration.
Treatment is explicitly in E1's pathway slice. The row's unit-bearing-leaf approach is appropriate, but treatment stage membership alone must not imply a clinical regimen or duration.
Observation is an optional stage; the current broad profile_use can imply it belongs to minimal, nominal, and surge scenarios. It also risks confusing ED observation with inpatient boarding.
recommendations.replacement: Keep pathways.observation optional and define its ED exit/return transitions; represent boarding separately from observation and include only when enabled in the profile.

recommendations.rationale: Reassessment is a conditional repeat stage rather than a universal step. The prior generic pathway statement does not identify its trigger or prevent an unbounded loop.
recommendations.replacement: Keep pathways.reassessment optional; require an explicit trigger/transition and bounded loop behavior in the profile, with any timing value as a typed duration.

recommendations.rationale: Consult is enabled only for some pathways. A candidate label across all profile types risks implying universal consult behavior, and no clinical consult rule is supplied.
recommendations.replacement: Keep pathways.consult optional; profile declares when it applies, the return/terminal transitions, and any resource claim independently.

recommendations.rationale: Discharge is a core terminal route in the generic patient pathway. The route key is appropriate if terminal reason and endpoint timestamps are retained for conservation and outcome summaries.
Admission route is valid, but E0/E1 distinguish provisional disposition from realized outcomes and require boarding behavior. The generic pathway rationale does not preserve that distinction.
recommendations.replacement: Keep pathways.admission; represent decision/provisional disposition, boarding occupancy, and realized admission as separate states/events, and do not treat an admission decision as ED exit.

recommendations.rationale: Outgoing transfer is a disposition route; the separate demand.transfers ID is incoming transfer arrivals. The matrix's generic route language should make direction explicit, and E0 freezes bed-offer and ambulance boundary assumptions.
recommendations.replacement: Keep pathways.transfer for outgoing transfer disposition only; state destination/eligibility and completion boundary, and do not conflate it with incoming transfer arrivals or imply a full fleet/ward model.

recommendations.rationale: Abandonment is a profile-specific terminal route, and the ID says so. The earlier rationale adequately preserves optional enablement and terminal accounting; keep it absent unless selected.

Routing probabilities are not generic policy values. The table must identify the decision point and conditioning population; simply saying conditional pathways are enabled does not define the routing denominator or relationship to deterministic routes.
recommendations.replacement: Keep pathways.routingprobability as an optional typed conditional table; bind each row to a named decision point, exhaustive/allowed outcomes, denominator, and deterministic-versus-probabilistic mode.

recommendations.rationale: The repeat-loop structure has no declared bound or cycle semantics. Generic candidate acceptance could permit infinite pathway execution or duplicate work without a model-level stop rule.
recommendations.replacement: Keep pathways.repeatloops only where enabled; require explicit loop edge, trigger, termination/max-iteration rule, and event accounting before a profile can use it.

recommendations.rationale: Priority policy is a Flow contract concern, and the prior recommendation correctly avoids choosing clinical priorities. Retain the key only when a profile uses multiple queue classes and bind ordering/tie-breaking to the reviewed queue contract.

Deadlines need explicit origin and absolute/relative form; the prior rationale states both and leaves tick conversion details to C0. Preserve that split and require an explicit missed-deadline behavior in the pathway contract.
A generic preemption flag would conflate staff-task interruption with patient/resource eviction. The prior rationale correctly separates them and limits MVP behavior to the reviewed queue contract.

Intrinsic work is active task time, not total elapsed patient time. Preserve that definition and do not fold queue wait, transit, or setup into this duration; distribution/value selection is outside this interface review.
Setup is a distinct duration, but the proposal does not state what is being set up or which resource/task owns it. Accepting a free-floating setup interval risks overlap with intrinsic work.
recommendations.replacement: Keep durations.setup only with an explicit task/resource owner and start/end event definition; state whether it occupies capacity and whether it precedes active work.

recommendations.rationale: Turnaround should represent process/device turnaround, with report availability and clinician review separated. The prior recommendation captures that distinction; duration semantics still need event boundaries in the typed consumer contract.

Report/review delay is a waiting interval after the relevant diagnostic process, not additional active work. The key is suitable if the model records report availability and review completion separately.
Cleaning affects when a location/resource is available again; the row does not say which resource's occupancy it follows. The broad duration wording leaves a capacity-accounting boundary unresolved.
recommendations.replacement: Keep durations.cleaning tied to an identified reusable resource/location and its release/ready events; avoid counting the same cleaning interval in both task work and resource availability.

recommendations.rationale: Handover is not a single universal interval: E0 calls out ambulance arrival, triage, handover, offload, and crew release as distinct clocks. The generic seconds-to-ticks rationale misses those separate endpoints.
recommendations.replacement: Keep durations.handover only for a named handover interval with explicit participants and start/end events; ambulance offload and crew release remain separate measures where modeled.

recommendations.rationale: Disposition duration is too broad to accept as an independent component while discharge, admission, transfer, and boarding routes already own elapsed work. The prior rationale notes overlap but does not resolve what this ID measures.
recommendations.replacement: Defer durations.disposition until E0 names the active interval, owning route, and endpoints; if it duplicates a route's active work or boarding, remove that duplicate representation from the profile contract.

cross_cutting_findings.finding: Rows 1–11 cannot share a single required-arrivals rationale: calendar modifiers, surge selection, case-mix dimensions, joint dependence, and boundary arrivals have distinct applicability and unresolved semantics.
cross_cutting_findings.disposition: Revise/defer the affected profile-use claims as recorded per row; retain the IDs and keys where useful.

cross_cutting_findings.finding: Rows 12–25 need stage- or route-specific applicability and transition boundaries; registration/triage/core pathway stages do not establish optional consult/observation/reassessment policy, admission realization, transfer direction, routing probabilities, or loop bounds.
cross_cutting_findings.disposition: Use the row replacements; do not infer clinical policy, values, or defaults.

cross_cutting_findings.finding: Rows 29–35 need interval ownership and non-overlap across active work, setup, turnaround, report/review, cleaning, handover, and disposition.
cross_cutting_findings.disposition: Accept only the stated typed interval boundaries; disposition duration remains deferred pending a concrete definition.
